title: Artificial intelligence-generated marathon training programs: reliable tools in exercise prescription for athletic performance?
authors: Montaruli G, Nikolaidis PT, Racil G, Maffulli N, Migliaccio GM, Padulo J
population: Outputs of eight AI models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet/Haiku, ChatGPT variants, Gemini 2.0 Flash variants, DeepSeek R1) each prompted for a 6-month marathon plan at beginner, intermediate and advanced levels
findings: Most AI systems identified weekly mileage progression, tapering and intensity distribution (>80% at low intensity), aligning with current endurance training theory.

Responses varied in accuracy and completeness: some omitted key details such as weekly mileage, merged intermediate and advanced levels as if the same, or gave inconsistent pacing data, especially for advanced runners.

The study is a descriptive qualitative comparison with the literature, not quantitative; authors note significant limitations in personalization and professional oversight and call for randomized trials including personal physiological data.
limitations: Descriptive and qualitative; 8 model outputs; no athlete outcomes; models are older generations than current.
implications: LLM output is inconsistent on mileage and pacing, supporting a validated deterministic engine with explicit numeric constraints.
Enforce level differentiation with explicit parameters (volume, long-run cap, quality-session count), not free text.
Use LLM output only as candidate text behind schema validation and rule checks.

verification.notes: Crossref: title, Br Med Bull, issued 2026-01-02, first author Montaruli match. PubMed/Europe PMC abstract (PMID 41722095) re-read in full.
